record.context_brief: Sub-exponential detection in hard synchronization regime
record.original_question: Consider synchronization over SO(2) or over a finite group, with signal elements sampled uniformly over group elements, and fix a number of frequencies L that does not depend on n. In the computationally hard regime lambda in (lambda_stat, 1), does there exist a sub-exponential-time detection algorithm, specifically running in time exp(n^delta) for some delta < 1, that can reliably detect the signal as n -> infinity?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8. Consider synchronization model over SO(2) or synchronization model over a finite group, where the signal x is sampled uniformly over group elements. Fix number of frequencies L that does not depend on n. In the computationally hard regime, i.e., when λ ∈ (λstat, 1), does there exist a sub-exponential algorithm, i.e., an algorithm running in time exp n^δ for some δ < 1, that can detect the signal reliably as n → ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let G be either the special orthogonal group SO(2) or a fixed finite group, and fix a positive integer L (the number of frequencies) that does not depend on n. Let ρ_1, …, ρ_L be a fixed collection of (nontrivial) irreducible unitary representations of G of dimensions d_1, …, d_L. The (multi-frequency) group synchronization model is defined as follows. A hidden signal x = (x_1, …, x_n) ∈ G^n is sampled with each coordinate x_i drawn independently and uniformly from the Haar measure on G (or the uniform distribution on G when G is finite). For a signal-to-noise parameter λ > 0 and each frequency ℓ ∈ {1, …, L}, one observes the matrix

   Y^{(ℓ)} = λ · u^{(ℓ)} (u^{(ℓ)})^* + W^{(ℓ)} ∈ ℂ^{n d_ℓ × n d_ℓ},

where u^{(ℓ)} ∈ ℂ^{n d_ℓ} is the block vector with i-th block ρ_ℓ(x_i) (vectorized appropriately), and W^{(ℓ)} is an independent GUE-type Hermitian Gaussian noise matrix on ℂ^{n d_ℓ}. The detection task is to distinguish the planted distribution above from the null distribution in which Y^{(ℓ)} = W^{(ℓ)} for all ℓ, with vanishing total error probability as n → ∞.

Let λ_stat = λ_stat(G, L) denote the statistical detection threshold (so detection is statistically impossible for λ < λ_stat) and let 1 denote the spectral/easy-algorithm threshold. The "computationally hard regime" is the interval λ ∈ (λ_stat, 1), where detection is statistically possible but no known polynomial-time algorithm succeeds.

Question. Does there exist a sub-exponential-time detection algorithm — that is, an algorithm running in time exp(n^δ) for some δ ∈ (0, 1) — that, for every λ ∈ (λ_stat, 1), reliably solves the above detection problem with error probability tending to 0 as n → ∞?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Recent work establishes low-degree-polynomial lower bounds suggesting a simple spectral algorithm is optimal among algorithms running in time exp(Ω̃(n^{1/3})) for detection over finite groups and SO(2) with a constant number of frequencies, but a positive sub-exponential-time detection algorithm in the full hard regime λ ∈ (λ_stat, 1) is not established. The known algorithm covering the entire hard regime has exponential runtime.

status_evidence.title: Computational lower bounds for multi-frequency group synchronization
status_evidence.snippet: Assuming the low-degree conjecture, a simple spectral algorithm is optimal among algorithms of runtime exp(Ω̃(n^{1/3})) for detection from a constant number of frequencies over finite groups and SO(2).
status_evidence.claim: Low-degree lower bounds rule out sub-exponential algorithms of runtime exp(Ω̃(n^{1/3})) beating the spectral threshold, but do not resolve the existence question for general δ<1.

status_evidence.title: Detection in Multi-Frequency synchronization (problems 7-8)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem about sub-exponential detection algorithms in the computationally hard regime for synchronization over SO(2) or finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: The question is recorded as an open problem on the Randomstrasse 101 problem list.
